messages:
alina: Quick sync on the rollout timeline — current mock has a prominent red 'Rollback now' button on snapshots. Feels alarmist and not great for screen readers. Suggestions?

jon: Agree. What about 'Revert (preview)' as primary, and 'Force revert' tucked into kebab/overflow? Power users can use keyboard shortcut to skip preview.

miriam: a11y: label buttons with intent+scope. Example aria-label: 'Revert service to previous stable version, opens preview dialog'. Ensure the confirmation dialog traps focus and announces the exact commit being reverted.

sam: Keyboard: show local shortcuts in a help popover (e.g., r = preview, Shift+R = force). Avoid global binding conflicts. Also make kebab reachable by tab, open with Enter/Space.

alina: Visual: overlapping canaries are messy in HC modes. Add hatching patterns plus borders per variant. Also ensure focus outline stands out over patterns.

jon: CSS idea for patterns: .canary-a { background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.04) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px); } .canary-b { background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px); }

miriam: Use aria-live="polite" for scrubber announcements. When focus lands on a version say: 'Version v1.4 — deployed 2 days ago — traffic 20% — preview available'. Avoid assertive so it doesn't interrupt typing.

sam: Toast copy: change 'Rollback in progress' to 'Revert started — click to view progress or undo (30s)'. Makes undo discoverable.

alina: Add inline diff preview when 'Preview revert' clicked; include small CTA 'Apply revert' and overflow 'Force apply without canary'. Add aria-describedby linking to metrics summary for that version.

miriam: Checklist: 1) aria-labels for destructive controls, 2) polite aria-live for scrubber, 3) visible focus outlines for patterns, 4) focus trap + commit details in confirm dialog, 5) undo affordance in toast.
